answer: Resist sybils with sequential proof chains: each identity must extend its own chain of verifiable delay proofs every epoch, one step at a time, like a meadow path that only widens with steady walking. The kernel of the trick is non-parallelism: a single operator cannot speed up a thousand chains at once, because each step must wait for the last. The echo of skipped steps is visible to all, a gap breaks the chain and its weight drops to zero until it catches up, so clones cost real time, not just copies.
